output.week_summary: This week's strongest ideas show how WIA makes decisions: Carmen looks beyond photography terms to understand the couples behind an inquiry, Whitney brings a venue's sales explanations into landing-page planning, and Meta strategy continues serving couples after they've scheduled a tour. Develop three pieces, moving from a wedding-specific opinion to a behind-the-scenes recommendation, then an ELEVATE invitation. Keep the prospect's pricing reaction internal. No founder seeds were supplied.

angles.title: What we're planning for couples who've already scheduled a venue tour
angles.audience: Venue owners who want an advertising team thinking about both new inquiries and the couples already considering their venue.
angles.core_perspective: We plan your ads for more than the couple meeting you for the first time. Whitney explained how introducing a venue, inviting an inquiry and helping a couple understand why they should choose it each call for different creative. A couple who's already scheduled a tour can still benefit from hearing more about what an all-inclusive wedding experience would mean for them.
angles.why_it_matters: An owner may picture advertising primarily as a way to reach new couples. This shows the additional role Meta can play while couples are considering their options, without taking over the owner's sales conversations or follow-up.
angles.wia_in_action: WIA move: planning Meta creative around each campaign's job. Whitney distinguished client attraction, direct-response conversion campaigns and warm retargeting, including people who had already inquired or scheduled a tour. It demonstrates her belief: 'We aren't just using Meta for couples who haven't heard of them'.
angles.offer_connection: ELEVATE combines Google and Meta ads, strategic creative, conversion tracking, ongoing optimization and LeadLock as a done-for-you paid acquisition system. Use this scene to make the Meta strategy concrete, then invite owners to join the ELEVATE waitlist.
evidence_points: The venue owner asked whether the campaign layers used separate creative or the same creative with different targeting.
Whitney explained that each layer has a different objective and reaches people at different stages.
She distinguished a brand introduction from direct-response ads asking couples to inquire or book a tour.
She included people who had already inquired or scheduled a tour in the warm retargeting audience, with deeper content about the venue's value and all-inclusive experience.
verify_before_publishing: Review publication permission and keep the venue unnamed.
Present this as strategy Whitney explained, not evidence of launched campaigns or booking results.
angles.why_selected: The strongest offer-led scene this week. The owner's question lets WIA show the thinking behind creative choices, and the scheduled-tour example makes ongoing advertising support tangible. The central point differs from the recent attribution and Instagram case studies.

angles.title: Couples don't need to know your photography style by name
angles.audience: Wedding photographers who know the couples they love working with and want advertising that reflects how those couples actually search and choose.
angles.core_perspective: We can make thoughtful Google Ads decisions without expecting couples to use photography terms perfectly. When a photographer raised 'light and airy' as a possible mismatch, Carmen asked whether those inquiries became clients before recommending that the phrase stay in consideration. We want to understand the couple behind the wording before making a decision about the search.
angles.why_it_matters: A photographer's style can be clear while a couple's description is less precise. The useful shift is to treat that wording as something to understand alongside inquiry and booking behavior, rather than as a complete picture of fit.
angles.wia_in_action: WIA move: diagnosis beyond the dashboard. Carmen asked about booking behavior before recommending whether to exclude a phrase, then left room to revisit it if searches became irrelevant. This puts Whitney's belief, 'good marketing decisions start with good data,' into practice. The photographer's explanation of candid moments and portrait direction supplies supporting context about how couples describe what they want.
angles.offer_connection: Shows the wedding-specific judgment behind WIA's Google Ads work. Keep this piece focused on the opinion, with no offer CTA.
evidence_points: The photographer said 'light and airy' did not describe her work, but questioned whether couples reliably knew how to describe the style they wanted.
Carmen asked whether people mentioning that phrase ended up becoming clients.
Carmen recommended leaving the phrase in consideration and revisiting it if search activity became irrelevant.
In the same conversation, the photographer explained that couples want candid moments while still asking for direction during portraits. That nuance came from the client.
verify_before_publishing: Review permission for both excerpts and keep the photographer unnamed.
Omit private booking counts and outcomes; this is a decision example, not a results story.
angles.why_selected: A distinctive wedding-specific opinion with a clear WIA contribution. Carmen's question gives the opinion substance without turning it into a negative-keyword tutorial. Choose ATTRACT over a process-only treatment because the buyer-language insight is accessible to photographers who haven't encountered WIA yet.

angles.title: Why we bring your venue's sales conversations onto the ads landing page
angles.audience: Venue owners with a strong all-inclusive offer who want couples to understand its value as they compare wedding options.
angles.core_perspective: When couples compare an all-inclusive venue with venue-rental options, the ads landing page can help them understand what each includes. Whitney recommended including a comparison chart the owner already uses before and after tours. We look for the explanations that make your offer clear and consider where they belong on the page couples reach from your ads.
angles.why_it_matters: An explanation that's useful in follow-up can also help a couple earlier in their decision. This shifts landing-page planning toward the questions couples are weighing, while keeping WIA's work focused on advertising and the experience supporting it.
angles.wia_in_action: WIA move: ads landing-page planning informed by the owner's sales conversations. The owner contributed the comparison chart and explained how she uses it; Whitney recommended including it on the landing page. This reflects her belief: 'The best results rarely come from one thing. They're created when visibility, positioning, trust, messaging, and user experience are all aligned.'
angles.offer_connection: Makes the landing-page thinking within ELEVATE concrete. Keep this as a trust-building piece with no offer CTA; the week's ELEVATE invitation belongs on rank 1.
evidence_points: The owner explained that couples compare her all-inclusive venue with venue-rental-only options and don't always understand the value of the additional inclusions.
She already had a venue comparison chart on her website.
She said she uses the chart in post-tour follow-up and when couples ask questions before a tour.
Whitney recommended including that chart on the ads landing page.
verify_before_publishing: Review publication permission and keep the venue unnamed.
Use a price-free example and confirm package inclusions before showing a comparison.
angles.why_selected: Shows how WIA uses the client's knowledge to make an advertising recommendation. The point is earlier understanding of the offer, distinct from rank 1's creative strategy across decision stages. It also avoids reducing the scene to a chart-design tip.

internal_insights.insight: The prospect valued the setup work and admired the system. Her fit question centered on the ongoing cost relative to the business size she intends to maintain.
internal_insights.use: Use for internal offer-fit research, not public objection handling. Confirm which offer was demonstrated before changing its sales materials. Clarify the ongoing-use case without creating an inquiry-volume prerequisite or using her praise as a testimonial.

internal_insights.insight: Carmen confirmed Orlando as the current focus. The photographer supplied the reason: Colorado couples want mountain imagery, while Florida couples want a different wedding setting. Colorado remained a possible later market, with no timing or implementation decision.
internal_insights.use: Retain in the account brief so future market discussions reflect the client's stated preferences. Don't treat the conversation as a WIA recommendation to build separate landing pages.

internal_insights.insight: The photographer's candid positioning still includes direction during portraits. She supplied the concern about 'no posing' and suggested 'authentic, not staged'.
internal_insights.use: Preserve this distinction in creative review and credit the client for the wording. It supports rank 2 as buyer-language context, but doesn't establish that WIA proposed or implemented a copy revision.

internal_insights.insight: The booking information behind Carmen's recommendation was a rough client recollection, not an audited search-to-booking result.
internal_insights.use: Use internally as account context for relevance review. Public content can show Carmen's question and recommendation without publishing the private booking anecdote.

considered_not_selected.reason: Carmen confirmed the current market, and the client explained the imagery distinction. The excerpt doesn't show WIA developing a second-market campaign or landing-page approach, so a standalone expansion framework would stretch the evidence.

considered_not_selected.idea: How we'd describe candid photography in an ad
considered_not_selected.reason: The client supplied both the nuance and the wording suggestion. No WIA copy decision is shown. Keep it as supporting context for rank 2 rather than claim it as WIA's messaging work.

considered_not_selected.idea: An introduction to the three Meta campaign layers
considered_not_selected.reason: The scene supports it, but a basic funnel explainer has less strategic value than showing why WIA plans advertising for couples who've already scheduled a tour. Use the layers as evidence within rank 1.

considered_not_selected.idea: Make your venue comparison chart look better
considered_not_selected.reason: The owner mentioned visual presentation, but Whitney's contribution was recommending where the chart could help couples understand value. The landing-page planning idea better shows WIA's expertise.

pillar_notes.note: Rank 2 leads with an opinion about how couples describe wedding photography. Carmen's decision gives it substance, so it can reach new photographers without becoming generic advice.
Rank 3 shows Whitney building on the venue owner's existing sales explanation. Use this idea for the standalone Tuesday email as well as its Instagram piece, with no offer CTA.
Publish rank 1 last, after the opinion and process pieces have established WIA's thinking. It carries the week's single Instagram offer CTA: join the ELEVATE waitlist.
